items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] That was 51, 52, and 53. I see. Did you hear any bands in when you were over there, Monta? Or did you just go to work?

ctx.x: What did you teach? I taught Taylor and Tri-State College in the Orange. I see. I stayed there for three years. What years were those? Like a few months or three years.
That was 51, 52, and 53. I see. Did you hear any bands in when you were over there, Monta? Or did you just go to work?

Yeah. I go around and listen to bands in this French Quarter. Listen to that cellar stare at them there after I get off from work, you know, sometimes. See, I get off early, I say, I'm going to the French Quarter, listen to that some good jazz music. And what's that white band, the Orphanile, they've been a while in the Orange. Sharky? No, I've been a Sharky too. Dukes of Dixon Land? Dukes of Dixon Land, that was my favorite. They were good during that time. And Famous Doors. Yeah. Yeah, that's where they're…
